problem:
A particle $P$ is moving in the $x$-$y$ plane. Its position vector relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}t),\,\sqrt{t+2}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=2.$

The speed at time $t=2$ is
{{field-1}}.

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Velocity for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+2),\,\frac{4}{t}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed $|v|$ of the particle at time $t=2.$ Do not round the answer.

The speed at time $t=2$ is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+2)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t+2},\,-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=2,$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =⟨\frac{1}{2+2},\,-\frac{4}{{2}^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{4},\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=2$ we calculate the magnitude of $v(2),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(2)| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{16}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{17}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{17}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
